statement: In a given circle to inscribe an equilateral and equiangular hexagon.
heath_proof: Let ABCDEF be the given circle; thus it is required to inscribe an equilateral and equiangular hexagon in the circle ABCDEF. Let the diameter AD of the circle ABCDEF be drawn; let the centre G of the circle be taken, and with centre D and distance DG let the circle EGCH be described; let EG, CG be joined and carried through to the points B, F, and let AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, FA be joined. I say that the hexagon ABCDEF is equilateral and equiangular. For, since the point G is the centre of the circle ABCDEF, GE is equal to GD. Again, since the point D is the centre of the circle GCH, DE is equal to DG. But GE was proved equal to GD; therefore GE is also equal to ED; therefore the triangle EGD is equilateral; and therefore its three angles EGD, GDE, DEG are equal to one another, inasmuch as, in isosceles triangles, the angles at the base are equal to one another. [I. 5] And the three angles of the triangle are equal to two right angles; [I. 32] therefore the angle EGD is one-third of two right angles. Similarly, the angle DGC can also be proved to be onethird of two right angles. And, since the straight line CG standing on EB makes the adjacent angles EGC, CGB equal to two right angles, therefore the remaining angle CGB is also one-third of two right angles. Therefore the angles EGD, DGC, CGB are equal to one another; so that the angles vertical to them, the angles BGA, AGF, FGE are equal. [I. 15] Therefore the six angles EGD, DGC, CGB, BGA, AGF, FGE are equal to one another. But equal angles stand on equal circumferences; [III. 26] therefore the six circumferences AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, FA are equal to one another. And equal circumferences are subtended by equal straight lines; [III. 29] therefore the six straight lines are equal to one another; therefore the hexagon ABCDEF is equilateral. I say next that it is also equiangular. For, since the circumference FA is equal to the circumference ED, let the circumference ABCD be added to each; therefore the whole FABCD is equal to the whole EDCBA; and the angle FED stands on the circumference FABCD, and the angle AFE on the circumference EDCBA; therefore the angle AFE is equal to the angle DEF. [III. 27] Similarly it can be proved that the remaining angles of the hexagon ABCDEF are also severally equal to each of the angles AFE, FED; therefore the hexagon ABCDEF is equiangular. But it was also proved equilateral; and it has been inscribed in the circle ABCDEF. Therefore in the given circle an equilateral and equiangular hexagon has been inscribed.

**Step 1.** Let ABCDEF be the given circle. Find its centre G (3.1). Take any point A on the circumference, join AG (P1) and produce it to meet the circumference again at D (P2); then AD is a diameter of the circle ABCDEF (D1.17).

**Step 2.** With centre D and distance DG describe the circle EGCH (P3), and let it cut the circle ABCDEF at the points E and C. Join EG and CG (P1) and produce them to meet the circumference of the circle ABCDEF at the points B and F respectively (P2). Join AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, FA (P1).

**Step 3.** Since G is the centre of the circle ABCDEF, GE is equal to GD (D1.15). Since D is the centre of the circle EGCH, DE is equal to DG (D1.15). Therefore GE is equal to ED (CN1), so the three sides GE, ED, DG of the triangle EGD are equal to one another, and the triangle EGD is equilateral (D1.20).

**Step 4.** Since GE is equal to GD, the angles GED and GDE at the base ED are equal to one another (1.5); since DE is equal to DG, the angles DEG and DGE at the base EG are equal to one another (1.5). Therefore the three angles EGD, GDE, DEG are equal to one another (CN1).

**Step 5.** The three angles of the triangle EGD are together equal to two right angles (1.32). Since they are equal to one another, the angle EGD is one third of two right angles.

**Step 6.** In the same way, GC is equal to GD and DC is equal to DG (D1.15), so GC is equal to CD (CN1), the triangle DGC is equilateral (D1.20), its three angles are equal to one another (1.5, CN1), and they are together equal to two right angles (1.32); hence the angle DGC is also one third of two right angles.

**Step 7.** Since the straight line CG set up on the straight line EB makes the adjacent angles EGC, CGB together equal to two right angles (1.13), and the angle EGC, being composed of the angles EGD and DGC, is two thirds of two right angles, the remaining angle CGB is also one third of two right angles (CN3). Therefore the angles EGD, DGC, CGB are equal to one another (CN1).

**Step 8.** The straight lines AD and EB cut one another at G, so the vertical angles BGA and EGD are equal; the straight lines AD and CF cut one another at G, so the vertical angles AGF and DGC are equal; and the straight lines EB and CF cut one another at G, so the vertical angles FGE and CGB are equal (1.15). Therefore the six angles EGD, DGC, CGB, BGA, AGF, FGE are equal to one another (CN1).

**Step 9.** In a circle equal angles at the centre stand on equal circumferences (3.26). Therefore the six circumferences ED, DC, CB, BA, AF, FE are equal to one another.

**Step 10.** In a circle equal circumferences are subtended by equal straight lines (3.29). Therefore the six straight lines ED, DC, CB, BA, AF, FE are equal to one another; hence the hexagon ABCDEF is equilateral.

**Step 11.** Since the circumference FA is equal to the circumference ED, let the circumference ABCD be added to each; then the whole circumference FABCD is equal to the whole circumference EDCBA (CN2). The angle FED stands on the circumference FABCD, and the angle AFE stands on the circumference EDCBA; therefore the angle AFE is equal to the angle FED (3.27).

**Step 12.** In the same way each of the remaining angles of the hexagon ABCDEF stands on a circumference composed of four of the six equal circumferences, so all these circumferences are equal to one another (CN2), and the angles standing on them are equal to one another (3.27). Therefore the hexagon ABCDEF is equiangular.

**Step 13.** The hexagon ABCDEF is therefore both equilateral and equiangular, and since each of its angles lies at one of the points A, B, C, D, E, F on the circumference of the given circle, it is inscribed in the circle ABCDEF (D4.3). Therefore in the given circle an equilateral and equiangular hexagon has been inscribed. Q.E.F.
